title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a programmatic 'Résumé' opening a section that follows a page headed 'Sorites sur VA, Picard, Albanese'.

Setting. k is an algebraically closed field. The parenthesis probably reads 'alg. clos pour fixer les idées', with finite fields perhaps also allowed. To a smooth projective variety X one attaches two abelian varieties built from cycles algebraically equivalent to 0:
- B_X = Pic^0_X ('Picard généralisé'), built from divisors;
- A_X = Alb_X, built from 0-cycles of degree 0 via the Albanese map.

The map u_Z. Let A be either of these for X and B either for Y; this gives 4 = 2×2 cases. Let Z be an algebraic cycle on X×Y of suitable dimension. Then ξ ↦ Z(ξ) = pr_{2*}(Z · pr_1^*ξ) sends cycles algebraically equivalent to 0 to cycles algebraically equivalent to 0, giving a group map A(k) → B(k). The suitable codimension of Z depends on the case:
- 0-cycles → 0-cycles: Z of dimension dim X;
- divisors → divisors: Z of dimension dim Y;
- the two mixed cases: the corresponding mixed dimensions.

Claims announced (to be proved later in the notes):
1. The map is induced by a homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A → B, which depends only on the numerical equivalence class of Z.
2. Converse: with Q-coefficients, every element of Hom(A,B)⊗Q arises from some Q-cycle Z.
3. ℓ-adic reformulation: the maps H^1(B,Q_ℓ) → H^1(A,Q_ℓ) coming from Q-homomorphisms A → B are exactly those induced by algebraic Q-cycles on X×Y. This uses the identifications H^1(Alb_T) ≅ H^1(T) and H^1(Pic^0_T) ≅ H^{2n-1}(T)(n-1), with n = dim T.

In short, the H^1 / H^{2n-1} part of correspondence theory is fully 'motivic'. The algebraicity of a cohomological correspondence on these Künneth components is equivalent to its coming from Hom of abelian varieties, the Tate-type statement for H^1.

Where it leads. The next page draws the consequence. If a Q-cycle induces an isomorphism on these H^1-type groups, the inverse isomorphism is also induced by a Q-cycle. Applied to cup product with ample classes ξ_1⋯ξ_{n-1} : H^1(X) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), this gives the Lefschetz standard conjecture B in degree 1 (algebraicity of the inverse Λ in degree ≤ 1). It also gives the independence of the H^1-part of correspondences from homological versus numerical equivalence. This page is the foundational input for the known low-degree cases of the standard conjectures.
errors: No genuine error on this page; the claims are correct (classical Weil–Lang–Matsusaka theory of correspondences plus Poincaré reducibility for the Q-converse).

Dependence only on numerical equivalence is asserted without proof here. It is true but non-trivial: it needs that homological and numerical equivalence agree on the relevant Künneth components, essentially via the Picard/Albanese theory itself.
The converse genuinely needs Q-coefficients (isogeny factors via curves / complete reducibility), as Grothendieck notes.

On the next page the identification for B_T is transcribed as H^{2n-1}(B_T) ← H^{2n-1}(T)(n-1). It should be H^1(B_T,Q_ℓ) ≅ H^{2n-1}(T,Q_ℓ)(n-1), since H^1(Pic^0_T) = H^1(T)^∨(-1). This is a slip or a misreading.

ideas.what: A correspondence Z on X×Y induces homomorphisms between Alb/Pic^0 of X and Y (four cases), depending only on the numerical class of Z
ideas.modern_name: Action of correspondences on Picard/Albanese; H^1-part of motives (Murre's Pic/Alb motives h^1, h^{2d-1})

ideas.what: Every Q-homomorphism A→B comes from a Q-cycle on X×Y; ℓ-adic reformulation: algebraic classes in the H^1-Künneth part of H^*(X×Y) = classes coming from Hom(Alb, Alb) etc.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear programmatic summary of the Picard/Albanese input to the standard conjectures. Its content (correspondences acting on Alb/Pic^0, the Q-converse, Lefschetz B in degree 1) is classical and appears in Grothendieck's and Kleiman's 1968–69 publications. Its interest is only as a record of how Grothendieck organized the material.
